text: Seat the integrated battery directly against the key carrier base to minimise tray height.

Keep the battery holder strong and narrow, with the pack lengthwise close to the rod seat and away from the fingers. For the integrated key carrier, use the contained-placement requirement rather than preserving projection beyond the carrier.
Hold the fitted pack against vertical movement when the wand is waved. Allow easy insertion and replacement without squeezing the pouch or loading its protection electronics.
On the integrated carrier, use a comfortable rounded slide-in friction fit for the fitted pack. Keep the pouch replaceable and secure when waved without squeezing it.

Taper the projecting outer edge of the integrated battery slot so that it does not extend as far as the rod-side edge. Replace the projecting outer right-angle corner with a diagonal taper. Keep the rod-side edge full length to retain the pack at the top.
Consider loading the battery with the rod out if necessary for compactness. Confirm actual removal access before adopting that dependency.
The bench assembly used a 100 mAh pouch. Use the fitted pack and its connector envelope when checking fit.
Integrate the pouch battery holder into the key carrier. Keep the separate rod-mounted battery holder available only for assemblies that use it.
The earlier assembly used an independently sliding rod-mounted battery above the keys, leaving the grip free. A later family revision integrated a different pouch in the key carrier.
Restore the integrated battery outer rail to its full pre-taper shape, retaining the lower battery support and the established removable fit. Keep unrelated current holder improvements.

Shorten the key holder above the hinge and keep only the battery rail length needed for secure removable retention. Preserve central insertion paths, pouch support and successful fitted friction without adding a separate cover. Use contained placement to minimise projection.
The actual R69 battery slides into its integral holder well. The user does not need an additional battery cover.

Move the integrated battery down the key carrier and outward as far as the fitted black hot-swap sockets, switch terminals, small body protrusions, wiring and complete assembly/removal routes permit. Unused key-opening space and decorative lightening holes may be overlapped or filled. Minimise projection beyond the carrier, clear the finger-guard beams and slim the outer rail while retaining safe pouch support, removable friction retention and rounded comfortable edges.

Keep the integrated battery at the R71 lengthwise position and depth. Move its seat toward the carbon rod as far as the socket, lead, guard and spring clearances allow. Keep the symmetrical top outline, slim rounded rails, secure removable friction fit and front stop.

Keep the R72 battery position beside the rod, the matching top tapers and removable friction fit. The wrapped pouch must slide all the way through the rails on a flat path. Keep printed stops, guard arms and pointed projections out of its path, including past the seated position. Keep its leads and connector accessible. Minimise the height and projections of the battery spacers against the fitted socket, solder and wires as well as the small switch pegs.

Insert the battery from its rail opening and remove it back through that opening. Preserve the flat rail bed, spring grip, accessible leads and rounded lips. A small projection at the battery end is acceptable. The space beyond the seated pouch at the click end belongs to the finger rest.

Bring the pack 0.8 mm closer to the keypad base than R77, accepting 2 mm more projection at the battery end. Move the rails to support this position. Blend the rail ends and remove redundant ledges and bumps. Keep the removable spring grip and clear the seated socket, solder and flat wire during rear insertion.
